title: Fwd Fuselage Frame Lower Web — Crack Stop Hole and Internal Strap Repair
abstract: Interim repair for a crack in the lower web of a forward fuselage frame between stations C36 and C44, using a stop hole set out from the corner fitting flange and an internal strap, valid until the next heavy visit.

sections.purpose: This repair arrests a crack in the lower web of a forward fuselage frame and restores the local load path with an internal strap, as an interim measure pending a permanent solution.
sections.damage_assessment: Confirm the crack length and both crack tips by eddy current inspection before anything is done. This repair is valid for a single crack up to 30 mm long in the web between the lower flange radius and the first fastener row, and only where both tips are clear of the flange radius. A crack that has entered the flange radius, a crack with more than one branch, or a second crack in the same web bay is outside the scope of this repair. Measure and record the distance from each crack tip to the corner fitting flange edge; the permitted stop hole position and the strap layout both depend on it.
sections.repair_procedure: Get access to the frame from inside the forward cargo compartment with the lower shell lining removed. Clean the web locally and mark both crack tips. Set out the stop hole positions from the machined edge of the corner fitting flange: three positions are permitted, at 24 mm, 38 mm and 52 mm inboard of that edge, and the stop hole must be at the first of those positions that fully removes the crack tip. Drill a stop hole of 4.8 mm at each tip and ream the hole to a surface finish of Ra 1.6 or better. Do a dye penetrant inspection of both stop holes and confirm that no indication runs out of them. Cut the internal strap to the layout of the repair drawing and dress the edges. Drill the strap fastener pattern into the lower web D5321117734118 using the strap as a template, keeping the pattern clear of the existing frame fasteners by the distance given on the drawing. Deburr, apply the surface protection of the standard practice and install the strap wet with sealant using solid countersunk rivets AES645587-2A. Restore the sealant fillet along the strap edge and around each stop hole.
sections.inspection_requirements: This is an interim repair and is life limited to 6 000 flight cycles from embodiment, after which a permanent repair or a frame replacement is required. Do a repeat eddy current inspection of both stop holes and of the strap perimeter every 1 500 flight cycles. Report the repair to Aeralis with the crack map and both stop hole positions. Any growth from a stop hole invalidates the repair immediately and the aircraft must not be dispatched until an engineering assessment is received.

type_data.allowable_damage_limits: One crack up to 30 mm in the web between the lower flange radius and the first fastener row, with both tips clear of the flange radius and no branching.

abstract: Interim repair for a crack in the lower web of a forward fuselage frame between stations C36 and C44, using a stop hole and an internal strap, valid until the next heavy visit.
